Population and comparison: All annotation-eligible tissue within stated distance bands, with missing annotations, source tissue layers and near/far coverage reported.
Interpretation when support is limited: Bands without sufficient tissue yield no estimate. Layer differences contribute to the measured mixture; a within-layer comparison, where annotations permit, targets a different population.

Population and comparison: A selected domain defined by its selection rule, connectivity, whole-domain annotation purity, tissue context and coverage in both bands.
Interpretation when support is limited: A fixed coverage-qualified rule identifies an eligible candidate where one exists; otherwise the regional estimate is unavailable. A disconnected union defines a separate sampling target.

Scientific target: Reference tissue for comparisons among specimens
Population and comparison: Broad profiles compared under the relevant specimen design, with identical patients across technical and modeled-composition controls and achieved balance reported.
Interpretation when support is limited: The supported patient and tissue subset and failed controls define the comparison. Patient- or control-dependent agreement calls for a comparator justified by its biological role rather than a universal near/far default.
